page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, delivering 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading. Memory is configured at 64 GB, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction flags include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI. The server contains no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, operating with 16 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily within the average performance band across standardized compute and memory evaluations. The system achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 31104.89, a Geekbench multi-core score of 13347.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 36657.12. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 151.74 GB/sec, while write operations measured 66.82 GB/sec. In application-level benchmarks, static web serving registered 33.38 GB/sec and Redis SET operations hit 31.2 million operations per second. Machine learning benchmarks showed small-model (135M) text generation throughput of 310.19 tokens/sec, placing in the strong quartile, while 7B model generation achieved 18.57 tokens/sec.

The 1:2 memory-to-core ratio offers cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads where massive RAM arrays or local scratch disks would represent idle resource overhead. Because no local storage is bundled, storage performance relies on network volumes, and memory-constrained databases may face bottlenecks. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.8xlarge is appropriately matched to CPU-bound processing, software build and CI/CD pipelines, high-concurrency web tiers, and lightweight inference services.

There is no bundled local storage and no GPU acceleration, while baseline network throughput is rated at 16 Gbps. The processor incorporates AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI support alongside standard cryptographic instruction sets. Benchmark assessments reveal balanced multi-core throughput, including a PassMark CPU result of 36657.12, 33.38 GB/sec in static web serving, and 310.19 tokens/sec for small-model text generation.
